blocks.x: Did you have much contact with Earl Hines?
No because Earl, by the time I decided I was going to become a singer, Earl had

already left from around Pittsburgh, and I heard Earl Hines over the radio on some of those remote broadcasts from Chicago. And Claude Hopkins was out in Chicago too at the time. In fact, I always said that when Benny Goodman got his first radio commercial show, I think it was NBC, National Biscuit Company, or whatever, then he came on and right after then he would go off the air and we would get those remote broadcasts with Claude Hopkins and Earl Hines from Chicago. So I always said they was breathing down Benny's neck. We had been listening to them before Benny got his show, you know.

So that's when Benny went out and hired Fletcher Henderson and you know, arrangers there. Because they was really breathing down Benny's neck. I mean, Benny is the band leader, it was a good band. But we've been listening to some good music before we heard that broadcast. I know that Benny was with some bands before he got his own band, promoted him as the king of swing because we used to hear bands like Ben Pollack on the radio. In fact I think Ben Pollack probably played Pittsburgh and I probably met him there.
